A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Associative Transformer. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support a reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and Sort-of-CLEVR experiments, component ablations, and analyses of attention, memory initialization, and Hopfield energy.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds ImageNet100 evaluation, further model comparisons, and additional ablations.

M1.justification: The specified memory-attention computation in Section 3.2 drops v3's separate W_Q query projection, also absent from v4's Algorithm 1. The main memory, bottleneck, balance-loss, and single-step Hopfield architecture remains. v3's explicit reconstruction-plus-input output equation disappears, but Figure 1 retains block residuals, so removal of all residual connections is not established.

E1.justification: v4 adds ImageNet100 classification in Section 4.2 and Table 2, extending natural-image coverage while retaining CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Triangle, Oxford Pet, and Sort-of-CLEVR. CLEVR and bAbI are future-work suggestions, not additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: v4 adds ViT-Medium to the existing classification comparison in Table 1 and the Oxford Pet comparison in Figure 2. Its relational comparison adds ViT-Base, ViT-Medium, and ViT-Small, absent from v3's corresponding Table 5. The other existing comparator families remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported EWMA smoothing factor from 0.9 to 0.1; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun. v4 also extends FLOPs measurement across classification comparators and introduces a test-time cross-attention disabling protocol in Appendix F, using AiT-Medium for classification and AiT-Small for reasoning.

E4.justification: v4 adds a direct W/O Attention Balance Loss ablation and removes v3's W/O FF ablation. New Appendix F tests whether cross-attention remains useful during inference. Existing memory-initialization, component-efficiency, prior-specialization, attention-sparsity, and Hopfield-temperature analyses are largely retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v4 systematically adds ± entries to classification, component-ablation, and memory-initialization tables whose v3 counterparts contained point estimates, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting beyond existing plot shading. Both versions still report means of three experiments. v4 does not define the ± statistic or establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v4 substantially expands reported outcomes with ImageNet100 results, additional ViT and AiT-Medium comparisons, comparator FLOPs, and new ablation results. For example, Table 2 reports 36.72% for AiT-Medium on ImageNet100. Most matched earlier scores remain, but AiT-Base's Triangle accuracy changes from 99.59% to 99.64%, and its average from 81.94% to 81.95%. W/O FF results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the formal memory-attention mapping by omitting the W_Q factor. Otherwise, the EWMA and balance-loss equations are mainly regrouped or reindexed, and Hopfield energy is rewritten in batched notation. Algorithm 1 consolidates existing operations; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 claims a new overall Sort-of-CLEVR SOTA in its abstract and conclusion. v4 narrows this to outperforming SOTA sparse Transformer comparators and removes the overall-SOTA assertion from the conclusion. The central contributions involving specialized priors, Hopfield retrieval, and parameter efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds discussion of layer-dependent bottleneck capacity for deeper models, contrasts AiT's processing with CNN+LSTM's modality-specific assumptions, and identifies potential Trojan-sample attacks exploiting sparse attention. The general scaling limitation and proposed adaptive temperature tuning already appeared in v3.

D1.justification: v4 adds Algorithm 1 and ImageNet100 hyperparameters in Appendix C. It removes v3's explicit test batch size of one and its disclosure of CLS-token removal with pooled classification representations. Frozen evaluation memory is retained in Section 3.2; hardware and the promise of future public code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds relational-reasoning references, including Compositional Attention and Slot Abstractors, plus ImageNet and bAbI references. Pyramid Vision Transformer and LeViT references disappear with the CLS discussion. It also removes the assertion that Coordination's evaluation was restricted to simple tasks; the broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes extensive rewriting, particularly the abstract, introduction, method overview, and experimental discussion, with systematic replacement of patch terminology by token terminology. Memory initialization and parameter-efficiency subsections exchange order, new appendix sections are integrated, and affiliations, acknowledgments, and citation style are revised.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reformats the document and tables, adds Tables 2 and 9 and Algorithm 1, expands the main comparison with a FLOPs column, and widens the ablation table. Figure 1 is revised and Figure 2 gains a ViT-Medium curve. v3's main-text prior-attention visualization moves to Appendix G as Figure 8; most other appendix graphics retain their underlying evidence.

improvement.justification: The ImageNet100 and ViT reasoning comparisons, targeted ablations, and narrower Sort-of-CLEVR claim strengthen empirical support and claim calibration. Algorithm 1 and table uncertainty entries also aid inspection. These gains are limited by undefined ± statistics, lost test-batch and readout details, and a new FLOPs inconsistency: Section 4.2 assigns ViT-Base 5.77 × 10^9 FLOPs, whereas Table 1 reports 5.60 × 10^9.
